relevance_reason: The paper is the original report linking heterozygous SEC61A1 mutations to primary antibody deficiency (CVID15). It includes the clinical findings, linkage results, the variants and the functional studies.

findings.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) studied 10 individuals in a family (Family I) with antibody isotype deficiencies involving IgM, IgG and IgA and severe recurrent bacterial infections, including tonsillitis, otitis, sinusitis, pneumonia and gastrointestinal infections. Onset was mostly in the first year of life. Affected individuals did not respond to polysaccharide vaccination and responded variably to tetanus toxoid vaccination. Infections became markedly fewer and less severe after IVIG replacement therapy was started.
quotes: We investigated 10 individuals in Family I (Figure 1A), who had antibody isotype deficiencies involving IgM, IgG and IgA (Table S1) and who suffered from severe recurrent bacterial infections such as tonsillitis, otitis, sinusitis, pneumonias and gastrointestinal infections.
The disease onset was mostly in the first year of life. Affected individuals did not respond to polysaccharide vaccination and responded variably to tetanus toxin vaccination (Table S1).

phenotypes.hpo_label: Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract
Decreased specific antibody response to unconjugated polysaccharide vaccine

findings.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) described Family II, in which the index patient (II.P3) was an 8-year-old boy with hypogammaglobulinemia since birth. With IVIG treatment he had no severe or recurrent infections, but repeated attempts to withdraw IVIG failed because his Ig levels stayed low. His grandmother, a mutation carrier, had more frequent upper respiratory infections and recurrent bilateral bacterial otitis media in childhood. At age 66 years her serum immunoglobulin levels were normal.
quotes: The index patient of Family II (Figure 1A) was an eight year old boy who had hypogammaglobulinemia since birth but owing to IVIG treatment has not experienced any severe or recurrent infections

His mother (who is affected by a secondary immunodeficiency and therefore not included in this study) and grandmother (II.P1) are also mutation carriers; the latter reported an increased frequency of upper respiratory infections during childhood with recurrent bilateral bacterial otitis media.
Now, at age 66, she has normal immunoglobulin serum levels (Table S1).

findings.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) found normal B-, T- and NK-cell ratios in patients from both families. T-cell subsets, regulatory T cells and recent thymic emigrants were normal. Peripheral B-cell subpopulations were also normal, including naive, unswitched memory, switched memory, transitional and CD21-low B cells. Only the very small CD27+CD38-high plasmablast population appeared reduced in Family I.
quotes: B-, T- and NK cells were present at normal ratios (Figure 2A and Table S4)
the peripheral subpopulations of B cells including naïve, unswitched memory, switched memory, IgA+, IgG+, transitional and CD21low B cells were also normal
Only the very small population of peripheral CD27+CD38high plasmablasts appeared to be reduced in patients of Family I (Figure 2B).

findings.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) performed a genome-wide linkage analysis with microsatellite markers in Family I and found linkage to chromosome 3 between markers D3S3697 and D3S3684. The peak LOD score was 3.31.
quotes: A genome-wide scan of all autosomes revealed only one region, on chromosome 3, with LOD scores greater than 2.
The peak single-marker and multiple-marker LOD score was 3.31. The genetic linkage analysis established that the mutated gene should be between markers D3S3697 and D3S3684 (Table S2).

findings.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) performed whole-exome sequencing on 4 affected and 2 unaffected members of Family I and identified a heterozygous c.254T>A transversion in SEC61A1, predicting a Val85Asp (V85D) substitution. SEC61A1 was the only candidate gene in the chromosome 3 linkage region, and Sanger sequencing confirmed that the variant segregated perfectly with the disease. V85 is highly conserved and is one of the 6 pore-ring residues of the Sec61 channel. In HeLa cells, the V85D mutant had impaired cotranslational translocation of preprolactin, and its overexpression lowered the ER calcium load, which the authors concluded was a dominant effect.
quotes: Evaluation of all variants shared among the four affected individuals and absent in the two unaffected family members revealed three novel single-nucleotide variants (SNV) in the genes SEC61A1, GOLGA8K and SLC47A2, with only SEC61A1 located in the linkage region on chromosome 3 (Table S3).
By Sanger sequencing we confirmed that the heterozygous missense mutation (c.254T>A, p.V85D) in SEC61A1 perfectly segregated with the disease within Family I (Figure 1B).
We observed that co-translational transport of ppl through the SEC61A1-V85D channel was significantly decreased compared to the transport through the wt channel (Figure 5B).

findings.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) carried out targeted next-generation sequencing in more than 200 additional patients with primary antibody deficiency and found a heterozygous c.1325G>T nonsense variant in SEC61A1 (p.E381*) in the index patient of Family II. His grandmother and mother also carried the variant. gnomAD contained no premature stop codons in SEC61A1. SEC61A1 protein was reduced in the patients' naive B cells, and no truncated protein was detected. The authors suggested that the variant causes nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and haploinsufficiency, with variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance.
quotes: We identified a heterozygous nonsense mutation (c.1325G>T, p.E381*) in individual II.P3 from Family II (SIFT score: 0.003).
there are no mutations reported in healthy individuals leading to a premature stop codon in SEC61A1.
supporting the hypothesis that the nonsense mutation p.E381* likely results in nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and leads to SEC61A1 haploinsufficiency in Family II.

findings.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) found that B cells from mutation carriers in both families made significantly fewer plasmablasts and plasma cells after in vitro stimulation, both T cell-dependent and T cell-independent, and produced less IgG and IgA. EBV-transformed B-cell lines from patients had less SEC61A1, lacked a CD38-high/CD138+ plasma cell subpopulation, and secreted less immunoglobulin.
quotes: The differentiation of resting peripheral B cells into CD27+CD38high plasmablasts and CD38highCD138+ plasma cells was significantly decreased in mutation carriers from both families upon T cell dependent (Figure 3A, B) and T cell independent (Figure S2A, B) stimulation.
we observed that all HD cell lines contained a subpopulation of CD38highCD138+ plasma cells that was absent in all patient-derived cell lines (Figure 4C).

findings.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) found that SEC61A1-V85D overexpression depleted the ER calcium store in HeLa cells, suggesting increased Ca2+ leakage. In multiple myeloma cell lines, stable expression of the mutant led to loss of the transduced cells and activated the terminal UPR, with upregulation of IRE1A, PERK, XBP1s, ATF4 and CHOP. Other cell lines were not affected. In thapsigargin-treated HEK293T cells, the V85D mutant had a dominant effect on XBP1s induction. The authors concluded that the mutation selectively impairs plasma cell survival.
quotes: the calcium load of the ER was significantly decreased in cells overproducing the mutant channel in comparison to cells overproducing the wt form (Figure 6C)
Taken together, these observations indicate that SEC61A1-V85D production selectively impairs the survival of plasma cell lines.

In addition to XBP1s, mRNA levels of ATF4 and CHOP were upregulated upon SEC61A1-V85D overexpression in L-363 cells (Figure 7C), pointing to the activation of the terminal UPR in this plasma cell line.

findings.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) suggested that SEC61A1 haploinsufficiency causes possibly transient hypogammaglobulinemia with variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance in Family II. In contrast, they proposed that the dominant-negative V85D missense mutation is responsible for the fully penetrant disease in Family I, which ranged from transient hypogammaglobulinemia and specific antibody deficiency to CVID.
quotes: We suggest that SEC61A1 haploinsufficincy is causing (possibly transient) hypogammaglobulinemia with variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance in Family II.

a dominant negative mutation in SEC61A1 resulting in a functional haploinsufficiency in combination with a dominant negative disturbance of the calcium homeostasis may be responsible for the fully penetrant PAD in Family I ranging from transient hypogammaglobulinemia and specific antibody deficiency to CVID.

findings.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) noted that the patients had no clinical symptoms other than infections. Serum levels of liver- and pancreas-secreted proteins were normal. Laboratory values that are altered in SEC61A1-associated ADTKD were also normal in these patients.
quotes: patients did not present additional clinical symptoms to infections and lab values of proteins secreted by the liver and the pancreas into the serum were all within the normal ranges (Table S5).
Laboratory values that were found altered in ADTKD patients were normal in our patients (Table S6).

relevance_reason: Mouse study of how XBP-1 deficiency affects plasma cell differentiation and antibody secretion. It includes no patients and no human variants, and the abstract does not link it to CVID15. It gives only context on antibody-secreting cell biology.

findings.statement: Taubenheim et al. (2012) studied XBP-1-deficient mouse B cells in vitro and in vivo. Antibody-secreting cells (ASCs) were still generated efficiently without XBP-1. In resting and immunized mice, ASCs were present at normal frequencies and showed the surface markers typical of plasma cells. Antibody secretion was reduced but not abolished, and the cells did not develop the morphology characteristic of ASCs. The authors concluded that plasma cell differentiation can proceed relatively normally without high rates of immunoglobulin secretion.
quotes: Using both in vitro and in vivo assays, we found efficient generation of ASCs in the absence of XBP-1.
ASCs were present at normal frequencies in resting and immunized mice and displayed a pattern of surface markers typical for plasma cells.
The absence of XBP-1 resulted in a reduction but not ablation of Ab secretion and the failure to develop the cellular morphology characteristic of ASCs.

relevance_reason: This is a mouse and in vitro study showing that the transcription factor XBP-1 is required for plasma cell differentiation and immunoglobulin secretion. It gives context on B-cell terminal differentiation, the step that fails in antibody deficiency. It reports no human patients or variants and does not link XBP-1 to CVID15.

findings.statement: Reimold et al. (2001) found that mouse lymphoid chimeras lacking XBP-1 had normal numbers of activated B lymphocytes, which proliferated, secreted cytokines and formed normal germinal centers. However, the chimeras secreted very little immunoglobulin of any isotype and could not control infection with the B-cell-dependent polyoma virus, because plasma cells were markedly absent.
quotes: Mouse lymphoid chimaeras deficient in XBP-1 possessed normal numbers of activated B lymphocytes that proliferated, secreted cytokines and formed normal germinal centres.
However, they secreted very little immunoglobulin of any isotype and failed to control infection with the B-cell-dependent polyoma virus, because plasma cells were markedly absent.

phenotypes.text: markedly reduced immunoglobulin of all isotypes
failure to control polyoma virus infection

findings.statement: Reimold et al. (2001) found that XBP-1 transcripts rose rapidly in vitro after stimuli that induce plasma cell differentiation and were present at high levels in plasma cells from rheumatoid synovium. Introducing XBP-1 into B-lineage cells started plasma cell differentiation. The authors concluded that XBP-1 is the only transcription factor known to be selectively and specifically required for terminal differentiation of B lymphocytes into plasma cells.
quotes: XBP-1 transcripts were rapidly upregulated in vitro by stimuli that induce plasma-cell differentiation, and were found at high levels in plasma cells from rheumatoid synovium.
When introduced into B-lineage cells, XBP-1 initiated plasma-cell differentiation.
XBP-1 is the only transcription factor known to be selectively and specifically required for the terminal differentiation of B lymphocytes to plasma cells.
